corrections.my_claim_1354: bounds.size_caps_bytes set audio=26214400 (25 MiB), document=26214400, video=52428800 (50 MiB), with the note that these 'sit at or below Telegram's own download ceiling so the cap is always ours and never inherited'.
corrections.correction: Wrong, and the note was self-refuting. Per official https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#file, the cloud download maximum via getFile is 20 MB. 25 MiB and 50 MiB are ABOVE that ceiling, so three of my caps were not 'at or below' it and the stated rationale was false.
corrections.corrected_rule: Two distinct ceilings, never conflated: (a) DOWNLOAD via getFile is capped by Telegram at 20 MB, so every UOS download cap must be strictly below 20 MB; (b) SENDING limits are different and larger and belong to the send path, not the download path.

corrected_download_caps_bytes.ceiling_note: All strictly below 20 MB under either the decimal (20000000) or binary (20971520) reading of '20 MB'. I do not assert which reading the API uses; the caps above are safe under both, which removes the need to resolve it. Precision I do not have is not invented.

corrections.root_cause: I asserted a relationship between my caps and an external limit without reading the external limit. Same defect class as my four earlier retractions: a claim whose evidence I never acquired.

corrections.my_claim_1354: 'telegram_call cannot carry an upload: a JSON `Assoc body cannot express multipart/form-data. A media send therefore needs a new, separate upload path and must not be bolted onto telegram_call.'
corrections.correction: Half wrong, and the wrong half is the expensive half. An EXISTING file_id can be sent as a plain JSON string field to sendPhoto/sendDocument/sendAudio/sendVoice/sendVideo. That path needs no multipart and works over the existing telegram_call `Assoc transport unchanged. Only a NEW binary upload requires multipart/form-data (https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sending-files).
corrections.corrected_rule: Split the send path in two. SEND-BY-REFERENCE (existing file_id, JSON, reuses telegram_call as-is) is cheap and is implementable now. SEND-BY-UPLOAD (fresh bytes, multipart) is the only part needing a new encoder.
corrections.consequence: T5 in the 1354 design was ordered last and marked conditional partly on this false premise. Corrected ordering is in corrected_task_order.

corrections.my_claim_1354: 'A media unit's identity is (update_id, message_id, file_unique_id). file_unique_id is the dedup key.'
corrections.correction: file_unique_id can neither download nor resend, and more importantly it identifies CONTENT, not a REQUEST. Keying request dedup on content collapses distinct operator intents: the same file forwarded by two users, into two chats, or as two separate requests, are three different things to do, not one.
corrections.corrected_rule: Two separate keys, never merged. REQUEST identity = (bot_identity, chat_id, from_user, update_id, message_id, request_intent) and flows through the existing ledger make_request_id / same_identity / watermark machinery. STORAGE identity = sha256 of fetched bytes, used only to avoid storing the same blob twice. file_unique_id is retained as a content correlation hint and is never an authority for either.
corrections.test_correction: 1354 test P-6 ('two different senders uploading identical bytes produce one stored object') is correct for STORAGE and must be paired with a new test: the same two ingests must still yield TWO distinct request records. Without that pair, P-6 alone rewards the bug.

corrections.my_claim_1354: Test N-9: 'Two different non-empty byte inputs to anything named with fft must produce different outputs.'
corrections.correction: That oracle is invalid. An FFT summary is a lossy, non-injective reduction; two different inputs legitimately CAN produce the same summary. My test would fail a correct implementation while only incidentally catching the current stub. I asserted a universal injectivity property of a transform that has no such property.
corrections.corrected_oracle: Known-fixture plus differential. (a) Synthesize a pure tone at a known frequency and assert the reported fundamental is that frequency within a stated tolerance; repeat for two or three known tones including one near a bin boundary. (b) Compare the summary against an independent reference implementation on the same fixtures. (c) Separately pin the stub's actual signature: assert that a correct implementation does NOT return a constant across the known-tone fixtures, which is a property of the fixtures, not a claimed property of FFTs in general.
corrections.note: The underlying finding stands and is unaffected: simulate_acoustic_fft branches only on byte_size > 0 and returns hardcoded constants. Only my test for it was wrong.

corrections.correction: That is a DEVELOPMENT invocation convenience, not an admitted production media daemon. Citing it as the production decode mechanism conflates the pattern with an admitted implementation.
corrections.corrected_rule: The PATTERN is correct and retained: media bytes are decoded in a bounded, timeout-enforced, reaped, supervised subprocess, never in the BEAM and never in a NIF. The IMPLEMENTATION is a new, separately admitted, OTP-supervised media daemon with its own two-key evidence, restart budget and resource bounds. The development launcher is the tool this REVIEW ran under; it is not the thing the design ships.

positive: S-P1: A send-by-reference of a known-good file_id succeeds over the existing JSON transport with no multipart encoder present.
S-P2: A send-by-upload of bytes within the send ceiling succeeds and the multipart body is well-formed (independent parser, not the encoder itself).
S-P3: A send is idempotent under the request key of C3: a redelivered send request sends once.
negative: S-N1: A send-by-upload above the send ceiling is refused BEFORE any network request; request counter must read zero.
S-N2: A send-by-reference with a file_unique_id instead of a file_id is refused with a typed error, because file_unique_id cannot resend (this is the C3 falsifier at the send boundary).
S-N3: No send path logs, spans or ledger rows contain the bot token or a /file/bot URL.
S-N4: A caption containing Markdown metacharacters cannot alter the sent message structure.
recovery: S-R1: A send that fails mid-multipart leaves no partial ledger row and is retried at most once under the request key.
S-R2: A restart during a send yields exactly one sent message or one reported failure, never two sends.
